# Developer Guide: Medical Lab Report Analysis System 

# 1\. System Overview & Architecture

This guide provides comprehensive technical documentation for developers to build, train, deploy, and extend the **Medical Lab Report Analysis System**.

The system solves two primary challenges in clinical document processing:

1. Eliminating numerical hallucination when extracting lab test values, units, and ranges.  
2. Generating patient-friendly, low-reading-grade summaries (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level \<=8.0) while executing locally on edge hardware to preserve Personal Health Information (PHI) privacy.

OCR_PDF_DPI=300

## 5.2 Pipeline Configuration

The .env values above map directly onto constructor arguments and constants inside the pipeline classes. The table below is the authoritative list of tunable knobs, where each lives in code, and what changing it does.

| Parameter | Location in code | Effect |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| text\_rec\_score\_thresh \= 0.30 | MedicalReportOCR (PaddleOCR init) | Drops low-confidence recognized text; raise to reduce OCR noise, lower to recover faint print |
| text\_det\_box\_thresh \= 0.40 | MedicalReportOCR (PaddleOCR init) | Detection box acceptance; controls how aggressively text regions are found |
| text\_det\_limit\_side\_len \= 1920 | MedicalReportOCR (PaddleOCR init) | Max image side fed to the detector; trades speed for small-text recall |
| upscale target \= 1800 px width | MedicalReportOCR.\_preprocess\_image | Images narrower than this are upscaled \+ CLAHE \+ sharpened before OCR |
| row tolerance \= 0.60 × height | MedicalReportOCR.\_make\_ordered\_lines | Vertical grouping tolerance when reconstructing rows from word boxes |
| chunk\_size \= 180 | ClinicalBERTNER.predict | Words per chunk; keep below the 256-token window to avoid truncation |
| max\_length \= 256 | ClinicalBERTNER.predict | Tokenizer max length per chunk |
| reference\_ranges | NERProcessor.\_\_init\_\_ | Per-analyte unit \+ normal (low, high); the HIGH/LOW/NORMAL flagging table |
| 4-bit NF4 \+ bf16 compute | BioMistralExplainer (BitsAndBytesConfig) | Quantization config for loading BioMistral-7B on limited VRAM |
| max\_new\_tokens \= 1024 | BioMistralExplainer.generate / chat | Upper bound on generated explanation / answer length |
| do\_sample \= False | BioMistralExplainer.generate / chat | Greedy, deterministic decoding (reproducible outputs) |

A convenient pattern is to centralize these in app/config.py and pass them into MedicalReportPipeline, so the same code runs identically in the notebook, the Streamlit app, and tests:

```shell
from dotenv import load_dotenv
import os
load_dotenv()
 
CONFIG = {
    "clinicalbert_path":       os.getenv("CLINICALBERT_MODEL_PATH"),
    "biomistral_base_id":      os.getenv("BIOMISTRAL_MODEL_PATH", "BioMistral/BioMistral-7B"),
    "biomistral_adapter_path": os.getenv("QLORA_ADAPTER_PATH"),
    "load_generator":          os.getenv("LLM_LOAD_IN_4BIT", "True") == "True",
}
```

# **6\.  Pipeline Architecture & Data Flow**

The orchestrator MedicalReportPipeline.process\_file() chains the four stages and returns a single result dictionary. The contract between stages is deliberately small — each stage consumes the previous stage's output and nothing else.

| Stage | Input | Output | Owner class |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 · OCR | Image / PDF path | Cleaned, value-only, lexicon-corrected text | MedicalReportOCR (+ filter, lexicon) |
| 2 · NER | Corrected text | Parallel lists of tokens \+ BIO tags | ClinicalBERTNER |
| 3 · Normalize | Tokens \+ tags | Structured lab\_results list \+ status flags | NERProcessor |
| 4 · Generate | lab\_results JSON | Patient explanation string \+ chat | BioMistralExplainer |

Stage 1 itself is a mini-pipeline: rotation correction → image preprocessing → PaddleOCR → row reconstruction → value-line filtering → lexicon correction. Each sub-step is a separate class so it can be unit-tested and swapped independently.

# **7\.  Module Reference**

Each class below is documented with its responsibility, key methods, notable parameters, and behavior. Signatures match the reference implementation in the notebook.

## **7.1  Stage 1 — OCR & Text Extraction**

### **7.1.1  EdgeBasedRotationCorrector**

Detects and corrects 90° page rotation using classical computer vision — no model required. It runs Canny edge detection, then a probabilistic Hough line transform, and classifies each detected line as horizontal or vertical by its angle (within ± 20°).

* detect\_rotation(image\_path) → int. Returns 0 or 90. If horizontal lines outnumber vertical by more than 2:1 the page is upright (0); if vertical dominate by 2:1 it is rotated (90); otherwise it defaults to 0.

* correct(image\_path) → (path, angle). Rotates with cv2.rotate when needed and writes the corrected image to the system temp directory, returning the new path and the applied angle. Failures fall back to the original image.

**Key parameters:** Canny thresholds (50, 150\); Hough threshold=100, minLineLength=30, maxLineGap=10; angle tolerance ± 20°.

### **7.1.2  MedicalReportOCR**

The core OCR engine. Wraps PaddleOCR and, critically, reconstructs table-like rows from the individual word bounding boxes so that a test name, its value, and its unit stay on the same line.

PaddleOCR is initialized for dense document print: lang="en", document-orientation / unwarping / textline-orientation classifiers disabled, text\_det\_limit\_side\_len=1920, text\_det\_thresh=0.25, text\_det\_box\_thresh=0.40, and text\_rec\_score\_thresh=0.30.

* extract(file\_path). Dispatches to image or PDF handling based on extension and returns the full reconstructed text.

* \_preprocess\_image(). Images narrower than 1800 px are upscaled (bicubic) and enhanced with CLAHE (clipLimit=2.0, tileGridSize=(8,8)) plus an unsharp mask; wider, already-sharp images are passed through untouched.

* \_make\_ordered\_lines(). Sorts recognized boxes by (y, x), groups them into rows using a vertical tolerance of max(10, 0.60 × row height, 0.60 × box height), joins each row left-to-right, and repairs common unit garbles (e.g. the OCR mangling of 10^9/L). Text below score 0.30 is dropped.

* extract\_text\_from\_pdf(). Uses pdf2image.convert\_from\_path to rasterize each page, then OCRs each page image.

* \_fallback\_ocr(). If PaddleOCR fails, falls back to pytesseract so the pipeline degrades gracefully rather than crashing.

### **7.1.3  ValueLineFilter**

Removes lines that cannot contain a lab result — letterheads, addresses, patient identifiers, page furniture — and keeps only lines that look like measurements. This dramatically reduces the noise the NER model has to reason over.

* A line is kept when it matches a value pattern (a number followed by a known unit, a numeric range like 13.0-17.0, or a comparison), or when it contains a known lab keyword together with a number.

* Skip patterns explicitly discard lab-branding and PII noise (lab names, addresses, “Sample Collected”, “Registered”, “Page”, and similar).

* filter\_lines(text) also normalizes recovered units on kept lines (e.g. gfdl. → g/dL, collapsing whitespace, tightening numeric ranges).

### **7.1.4  LexiconCorrectorAllTests**

Unit-safe normalization of analyte names to a single canonical vocabulary. It applies an ordered list of \~180 case-insensitive regular-expression corrections that map synonyms, abbreviations, and common OCR misspellings onto one consistent name.

* Examples: hgb / haemoglobin → Hemoglobin, leukocytes / wbc → WBC Count, tsh → Thyroid Stimulating Hormone, and misspelling fixes like lymchecytes → Lymphocytes.

* Canonicalizing names before NER means the reference-range lookup in Stage 3 sees stable keys, which is what keeps flagging deterministic across differently-formatted lab reports.

* correct\_text() logs every substitution it makes and collapses accidental duplicate words, so corrections are auditable.

## **7.2  Stage 2 — Token Tagging (ClinicalBERTNER)**

Loads a fine-tuned ClinicalBERT token-classification model and tags every word with a BIO label. The label set distinguishes test names, values, and units: B-TEST, I-TEST, B-VALUE, B-UNIT, O. The model and tokenizer are loaded with local\_files\_only=True so inference is fully offline.

* predict(text) → (tokens, tags). Processes the text line by line. Each line is split into words and chunked at 180 words; each chunk is tokenized with is\_split\_into\_words=True and max\_length=256.

* **Sub-word alignment.** Only the first sub-token of each word carries the predicted label (via word\_ids()), so the returned tags line up one-to-one with the input words — no double-counting of word pieces.

* Runs on GPU when available, otherwise CPU; id2label is read from the model config so the class stays agnostic to the exact label ordering.

## **7.3  Stage 3 — Normalization & Aggregation (NERProcessor)**

Turns the flat (tokens, tags) stream into a clean list of lab results and — deterministically — flags each value against a hardcoded reference-range table. This is the stage that guarantees the numbers shown to the patient are the numbers from the report.

* **Entity assembly.** Consecutive B-/I- tags are merged into typed entities (TEST / VALUE / UNIT), then each TEST is paired with the first following VALUE and UNIT until the next TEST begins.

* **De-noising.** A skip-list drops spurious “tests” that are really headers or PII fragments (e.g. names, “SAMPLE”, “PAGE”, “REFERENCE”), and duplicate tests are removed.

* **Name canonicalization.** Variants are mapped to canonical test names (e.g. packed-cell-volume → HCT / Hematocrit, differential absolutes normalized).

* **Reference-range flagging.** Each value is parsed to a float and compared against the analyte's normal (low, high) band, yielding a status of NORMAL, HIGH, LOW, or UNKNOWN (when no range is known or the value can't be parsed). Missing units are backfilled from the range table.

The shipped range table covers the complete-blood-count (CBC) panel. It is the primary extension point (Section 11):

| Analyte | Unit | Normal (low–high) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| WBC / WBC Count | 10^9/L | 4.0 – 11.0 |
| Hemoglobin | g/dL | 13.0 – 17.0 |
| Hematocrit (HCT) | % | 40.0 – 50.0 |
| Platelet Count | 10^9/L | 150 – 450 |
| MCV | fL | 83.0 – 101.0 |
| MCH | pg | 27.0 – 32.0 |
| MCHC | g/dL | 31.5 – 34.5 |
| RDW | % | 11.5 – 14.5 |
| Neutrophils / Lymphocytes | % | 40–80 / 20–40 |
| Eosinophils / Basophils / Monocytes | % | 1–6 / 0–2 / 2–10 |
| Absolute Neutrophils | cells/mcL | 1500 – 7500 |
| Absolute Lymphocytes | cells/mcL | 1300 – 3500 |
| Absolute Eosinophils / Monocytes / Basophils | cells/mcL | 0–500 / 200–950 / 0–300 |

## **7.4  Stage 4 — Patient-Facing Generation (BioMistralExplainer)**

Loads BioMistral-7B in 4-bit and turns the Stage 3 lab\_results JSON into a plain-English explanation. An optional fine-tuned LoRA adapter is attached on top of the base model for the low-reading-grade patient style.

**Quantization.** Loaded with BitsAndBytesConfig(load\_in\_4bit=True, bnb\_4bit\_quant\_type="nf4", bnb\_4bit\_compute\_dtype=torch.bfloat16, bnb\_4bit\_use\_double\_quant=True) and device\_map="auto".

* generate(lab\_results) → str. Single-turn, stateless. Serializes the results to JSON, applies the chat template, and decodes greedily (do\_sample=False, max\_new\_tokens=1024) — deterministic output for the same input.

* chat(prompt, reset=False) → str. Multi-turn follow-up. Maintains conversation\_history across calls so a patient can ask questions about their report; pass reset=True to seed a fresh conversation from the results JSON.

* reset\_chat(). Clears the running conversation history.

## **7.5  Orchestration (MedicalReportPipeline)**

Constructs every stage once and exposes a single process\_file(path) entry point. Stage 4 is optional: if load\_generator=False (or the generator fails to load) the pipeline returns Stages 1–3 and skips explanation, so the system still works on CPU-only hosts.

| PYTHON class MedicalReportPipeline:     def \_\_init\_\_(self, clinicalbert\_path,                  biomistral\_base\_id="BioMistral/BioMistral-7B",                  biomistral\_adapter\_path=None,                  load\_generator=True):         self.ocr       \= MedicalReportOCR()         self.filter    \= ValueLineFilter()         self.lexicon   \= LexiconCorrectorAllTests()         self.ner       \= ClinicalBERTNER(clinicalbert\_path)         self.processor \= NERProcessor()         self.generator \= (BioMistralExplainer(biomistral\_base\_id,                           biomistral\_adapter\_path) if load\_generator else None)       def process\_file(self, file\_path) \-\> dict:         raw       \= self.ocr.extract(file\_path)          \# Stage 1         filtered  \= self.filter.filter\_lines(raw)         corrected \= self.lexicon.correct\_text(filtered)         tokens, tags \= self.ner.predict(corrected)       \# Stage 2         result \= self.processor.process(tokens, tags)    \# Stage 3         if self.generator:                               \# Stage 4             result\["patient\_explanation"\] \= self.generator.generate(result\["lab\_results"\])         return result |
| :---- |

**Robustness.** At each boundary the orchestrator short-circuits with a structured failure result (success=False plus a human-readable message) if the previous stage produced nothing — no text extracted, no tokens, or no lab results — rather than raising.

# **8\.  Running the Pipeline**

## **8.1  Programmatic Usage**

Set the four paths, build the pipeline, and process a file. Set LOAD\_GENERATOR \= False to run Stages 1–3 only (no GPU needed).

| PYTHON INPUT\_FILE              \= "path/to/report.png"     \# image or PDF CLINICALBERT\_PATH       \= "path/to/clinicalbert\_ner\_model" BIOMISTRAL\_BASE\_ID      \= "BioMistral/BioMistral-7B" BIOMISTRAL\_ADAPTER\_PATH \= "path/to/biomistral-lab-explainer-lora-final"  \# or None LOAD\_GENERATOR          \= True   pipeline \= MedicalReportPipeline(     clinicalbert\_path=CLINICALBERT\_PATH,     biomistral\_base\_id=BIOMISTRAL\_BASE\_ID,     biomistral\_adapter\_path=BIOMISTRAL\_ADAPTER\_PATH,     load\_generator=LOAD\_GENERATOR, ) result \= pipeline.process\_file(INPUT\_FILE) |
| :---- |

## **8.2  Inspecting Results**

| PYTHON import json print(json.dumps(result.get("lab\_results", \[\]), indent=2)) print(result.get("summary", {}).get("text", "No summary")) if result.get("patient\_explanation"):     print(result\["patient\_explanation"\]) |
| :---- |

## **8.3  Conversational Follow-Up**

Seed the chat from the results JSON, then ask follow-up questions. The explainer keeps history between calls.

| PYTHON \# seed a fresh conversation from the structured results seed \= pipeline.generator.chat(json.dumps(result\["lab\_results"\]), reset=True) print(seed)   \# ask follow-ups (history is retained) print(pipeline.generator.chat("Which of my results are outside the normal range?")) print(pipeline.generator.chat("What could a high value here mean?")) |
| :---- |

## **8.4  Saving Output**

| PYTHON with open("pipeline\_result.json", "w") as f:     json.dump(result, f, indent=2) |
| :---- |

# **9\.  Output Data Schema**

process\_file() returns a dictionary with a stable shape. This is the contract the Streamlit scorecard and any downstream consumer should code against.

| JSON {   "success": true,   "lab\_results": \[     {       "test": "Hemoglobin",         // canonical test name       "value": "11.2",              // exactly as read from the report       "unit": "g/dL",               // read or backfilled from range table       "test\_name": "Hemoglobin",    // display name       "status": "LOW"               // NORMAL | HIGH | LOW | UNKNOWN     }   \],   "summary": {     "total\_tests": 12,     "abnormal\_count": 3,     "text": "Found 12 lab tests."   },   "patient\_explanation": "Your hemoglobin is a little low ..."  // or null } |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Field** | **Type** | **Meaning** |
| success | bool | False with an error message if a stage produced no usable output |
| lab\_results\[\] | list | One object per detected test |
| lab\_results\[\].value | string | Verbatim from OCR — never model-generated |
| lab\_results\[\].status | enum | NORMAL / HIGH / LOW / UNKNOWN from the reference-range table |
| summary.abnormal\_count | int | Count of HIGH or LOW results (drives the scorecard) |
| patient\_explanation | string | null | Stage 4 output; null when the generator is disabled |

# **10\.  Model Training & Fine-Tuning**

Two models are trained. Both training scripts live under training/. The base pipeline runs with the shipped fine-tuned weights; retrain only when adapting to new report formats or analytes.

## **10.1  ClinicalBERT NER (Stage 2\)**

A token-classification head is fine-tuned on lab-report text labeled with the BIO scheme (B-TEST, I-TEST, B-VALUE, B-UNIT, O). Training data is the value-filtered, lexicon-corrected text so the model learns the same distribution it sees at inference.

* Objective: token-level cross-entropy; evaluate with seqeval (entity-level precision / recall / F1).

* Keep the training tokenizer settings identical to inference (is\_split\_into\_words=True, max\_length=256, first-sub-token label alignment) to avoid train/serve skew.

| BASH python training/train\_ner.py \\     \--base\_model  emilyalsentzer/Bio\_ClinicalBERT \\     \--train data/train\_reports.csv \--val data/val\_reports.csv \\     \--labels B-TEST I-TEST B-VALUE B-UNIT O \\     \--max\_length 256 \--epochs 5 \--lr 3e-5 \\     \--output ./models/clinicalbert\_finetuned |
| :---- |

## **10.2  BioMistral QLoRA (Stage 4\)**

BioMistral-7B is adapted with QLoRA — the base weights stay frozen in 4-bit NF4 and only small LoRA adapters are trained. Use the identical BitsAndBytesConfig shown in Section 7.4 so training and inference quantization match.

* Input \= the Stage 3 lab\_results JSON; target \= a patient-friendly explanation written at FKGL ≤ 8.0. Score readability with the textstat package during evaluation.

* Recommended LoRA setup: rank r=16, lora\_alpha=32, dropout 0.05, targeting the attention projection modules; train with trl’s SFT trainer.

| BASH python training/train\_llm.py \\     \--base BioMistral/BioMistral-7B \\     \--data data/train\_reports.csv \\     \--lora\_r 16 \--lora\_alpha 32 \--lora\_dropout 0.05 \\     \--load\_in\_4bit \--bf16 \--epochs 3 \\     \--output ./models/biomistral\_qlora |
| :---- |

**Note.** The hyperparameters above are recommended starting points consistent with the inference configuration; tune them against your held-out test\_reports.csv and the FKGL target.

# **11\.  Extending the System**

## **11.1  Adding a New Lab Test**

Adding coverage for a new analyte is a three-touch change and requires no retraining for the flagging to work:

1. **Lexicon.** Add name variants / misspellings → canonical name in LexiconCorrectorAllTests.CORRECTIONS.

2. **Reference range.** Add an entry to NERProcessor.reference\_ranges with the unit and normal (low, high) band.

3. **Filter keywords (optional).** Add the test to ValueLineFilter.lab\_keywords so its lines survive filtering even without a recognized unit.

| PYTHON \# NERProcessor.reference\_ranges "FERRITIN": {"unit": "ng/mL", "normal": (30.0, 400.0), "name": "Ferritin"},   \# LexiconCorrectorAllTests.CORRECTIONS (r"(?i)\\bferritin\\.?\\b", "Ferritin"), |
| :---- |

The NER model already emits generic TEST / VALUE / UNIT tags, so a new analyte is picked up as long as its line survives filtering and its name canonicalizes — retraining is only needed if the model systematically mis-tags an unusual layout.

## **11.2  Other Extension Points**

* **Swap the OCR engine** by replacing MedicalReportOCR.extract() while keeping its str → text contract.

* **Change the explanation style** by training a new LoRA adapter and pointing QLORA\_ADAPTER\_PATH at it — no other stage changes.

* **Add report layouts** by extending ValueLineFilter.skip\_patterns with new letterhead / PII noise so it doesn't reach the NER model.

# **12\.  Testing & Validation**

Unit tests live under tests/. Because each stage has a small, typed contract, they can be tested in isolation with fixed inputs.

| Test file | Validates | Approach |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| test\_ocr.py | Rotation, preprocessing, row reconstruction | Feed known images, assert reconstructed lines & kept units |
| test\_ner.py | Token/tag alignment, chunking | Assert len(tokens) \== len(tags) and expected entities on samples |
| test\_pipeline.py | End-to-end schema & flagging | Run process\_file on fixtures; assert status flags & JSON shape |

**Recommended checks:** verify values are never altered between OCR and output (numerical-fidelity test), confirm HIGH/LOW/NORMAL against hand-labeled fixtures, and measure the patient explanation's FKGL with textstat to enforce the ≤ 8.0 target.

| BASH pytest tests/ \-v |
| :---- |

# **13\.  Deployment**

The system is packaged as a Streamlit app and shipped via Docker. Model weights are mounted (not baked into the image) so PHI-adjacent artifacts stay on the host.

## **13.1  Docker**

| BASH \# Build docker build \-t medical-report-analysis .   \# Run (GPU) — mount local weights and expose Streamlit docker run \--gpus all \-p 8501:8501 \\     \-v $(pwd)/models:/app/models \\     \--env-file .env \\     medical-report-analysis   \# Or with compose docker-compose up \--build |
| :---- |

## **13.2  Launching the App Directly**

| BASH streamlit run app/s\_app.py |
| :---- |

**Privacy posture.** All models run locally; no request leaves the machine at inference time. For production, terminate TLS in front of Streamlit, keep APP\_SECRET\_KEY out of source control, and mount weights read-only.

# **14\.  Troubleshooting**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| “PaddleOCR not available” | paddleocr / paddlepaddle not installed | Install the correct CPU or GPU Paddle build; re-check the import |
| No text extracted | Very low-res or heavily skewed scan | Ensure OCR\_ENABLE\_PREPROCESSING is on; increase source DPI; check rotation |
| Values on wrong lines | Row-reconstruction tolerance too tight/loose | Adjust the 0.60 × height tolerance in \_make\_ordered\_lines |
| Test present but status \= UNKNOWN | Analyte missing from reference\_ranges, or value unparseable | Add a range entry (Section 11); check the value string |
| FileNotFoundError on ClinicalBERT | Bad CLINICALBERT\_MODEL\_PATH | Point to the local model directory; it loads with local\_files\_only=True |
| CUDA out of memory (Stage 4\) | Insufficient VRAM for BioMistral-7B | Confirm 4-bit is active; free VRAM; or set LOAD\_GENERATOR=False |
| Chat unavailable | Generator not loaded or no lab\_results | Enable LOAD\_GENERATOR and verify Stage 3 produced results |
| Garbled units (10^9/L) | OCR mis-recognition of superscripts | Handled by built-in repairs; extend them in \_make\_ordered\_lines / filter |
